sections.h2: Why Florida exteriors fail, and where we start
body: Paint on a Florida house rarely fails evenly. The west and south walls chalk and fade years before the shaded north side. The bottom foot of siding takes rain splash and sprinkler spray and stays damp. Stucco opens hairline cracks as it heats and cools. Good exterior house painting in North Central Florida means reading those patterns on your house and pricing the fixes each wall actually needs.

On the walkthrough, a crew lead photographs every elevation, measures, and takes moisture readings on wood or stucco that looks suspect. The estimate then lists the repairs, products, and coats for your house rather than a flat number per square foot. For a deeper look at the wear pattern, read how long exterior paint lasts in Florida.

sections.h2: Prep: washing, repairs, and sealing the envelope
body: Most exterior failures start under the paint. Before we coat anything, the house is cleaned and the problems are fixed. Washing is done with the right method for the surface; see our pressure washing and soft washing service for how we treat mildew and algae without forcing water behind siding.
bullets: Wash and treat mildew and algae, then allow full dry time
Scrape loose paint and sand edges so new coats lie flat
Replace rotted fascia, trim, and siding boards rather than painting over them
Re-caulk gaps at windows, doors, and trim joints, and reset nail pops
Spot-prime bare wood and repaired areas
Mask windows, fixtures, hardware, plantings, and walkways

sections.h2: Coating systems for stucco, siding, and trim
body: We match the coating to the surface. Wood and fiber-cement siding and trim get 100% acrylic, which stays flexible through heat and resists UV. Stucco and block with hairline cracking get an elastomeric coating that stretches over small movement instead of telegraphing every crack. Front doors, railings, and shutters get a waterborne urethane enamel. Cracked or damaged stucco is repaired first through our stucco repair and painting service.

Products come from premium Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore lines and are named on your estimate. Two full coats is the baseline, and sprayed surfaces are back-rolled or back-brushed where the coating needs to get into texture or grain. Trim, shutters, and doors can also be refreshed on their own through trim and molding painting.

sections.h2: Surfaces we paint and what each one needs
body: Every exterior material behaves differently in our climate, so the prep and product change from house to house. Painted stucco is the most common surface we see in newer neighborhoods; it holds moisture after rain and grows algae on shaded walls, so cleaning and crack treatment come first. Lap and board-and-batten wood siding, common in older Gainesville and High Springs homes, needs careful scraping and spot-priming of bare wood. Fiber-cement siding holds paint well but needs every butt joint and trim seam caulked. Painted block and brick need a breathable masonry-appropriate system and attention to efflorescence.

Trim, fascia, soffits, garage doors, front doors, and shutters are part of nearly every exterior. These are the pieces people see up close, so they get extra care: sanded smooth, sealed at joints, and finished in a harder enamel where hands and weather hit them. If you are thinking about changing colors, our post on historic paint colors in Gainesville is a good place to start.

sections.h2: Weather, timing, and how long it takes
body: Our best exterior season is October through May, when humidity is lower and afternoon storms are less frequent. We do paint in summer, but crews start earlier in the day, watch the dew point so paint can form a good film, and stop when radar shows a storm coming. Painting through a summer afternoon to stay on schedule is how coatings get washed off or blister. Our article on how Florida weather affects house painting explains the details.

A full exterior typically takes three to seven working days, plus washing and dry time. Most projects start one to three weeks after you approve the estimate. You do not need to be home while we work outside, but we do ask that sprinklers be turned off for the wash and paint days, and that cars be moved away from the driveway side of the house.

Exterior projects carry a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years, on top of the manufacturer's product warranty. You sign the final punch walk, anything not right is fixed first, and labelled touch-up paint stays with you. We paint homes from Lake City to Belleview; see our Gainesville exterior painting and Ocala exterior painting pages for local notes.

faqs.q: How long does exterior paint last in Florida?
faqs.a: It depends on exposure, prep, and product. Sun-facing walls wear fastest. A well-prepped house with premium acrylic or elastomeric coatings holds up much longer than a quick one-coat job, and our exterior work carries a written warranty of up to 10 years.

faqs.q: When is the best time to paint a house exterior in Florida?
faqs.a: October through May is the best window in North Central Florida. Summer work is possible, but crews start early, watch the dew point, and stop ahead of afternoon storms.

faqs.q: Should stucco get elastomeric or acrylic paint?
faqs.a: Stucco with hairline cracks usually does best with an elastomeric coating, which flexes over movement. Sound, uncracked stucco can take a quality 100% acrylic. We decide after inspecting the walls and name the product on the estimate.

faqs.q: Do you fix rotted wood before painting?
faqs.a: Yes. Rotted fascia, trim, and siding boards are replaced as part of prep and listed on the estimate. Painting over rot only hides it for a short time.
